name: Fundamental Studies in Droplet Combustion and Flame Extinguishment (FLEX-2)
summary: Science requirements describe droplet combustion/extinguishment and fuel, oxygen fraction, ambient pressure, temperature and flow ranges.
insight: Ranges listed in the experiment table are planned/parameter ranges, not individual observed outcomes.

name: CLD Flame — experimental test table
summary: Experimental table contains methane-based test configurations, mass-flow-controller information, fuel concentration range and counts of ignited flames.
insight: Classification derives from gaseous flame test table; the precise premixed/non-premixed configuration requires further checking.

name: ACME — Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G)
summary: Final report identifies ACME/CFI-G, and its inverse-flame table records fuel, pressure, oxygen fraction, hydrocarbon burn rate, oxygen flow, ignition, burn time and burner temperature.
insight: Do not interpret a failed ignition row as a measured flame extinction event.

name: Combustion Behavior of Sub-Millimeter Sized Oxygenated and N-Alkane Fuel Droplets
summary: 2018 University of South Carolina dissertation on fuel droplets; supplementary analyzed data list fuels, initial droplet size, pressure, oxygen conditions and publication reference.
insight: No numerical flame-spread value was inferred from droplet measurements.

name: ACME — Flame Design
summary: 2023 ACME/Flame Design final report describes design and testing of diffusion flames with attention to soot, extinction and operating conditions.
insight: Measured outcomes must be traced to the relevant ACME test tables rather than inferred from the report overview.

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids (BASS)
summary: ISS 2013 BASS conference document describes investigation of burning and suppression behavior of solid materials.
insight: Separate from BASS-II; two identical copies of the BASS PDF are present in Drive.

name: ACME — Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (s-Flame)
summary: 2021 NASA final report describes spherical diffusion flames of gaseous fuels, experimental objectives and ISS operations.
insight: Report notes that analysis/publication of some results was ongoing at its issue date.

name: ACME — Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
summary: ACME E-FIELD Flames 30-day operations report covers electric-field effects on laminar diffusion flames during ISS increments 55–56.
insight: Telemetry files should not be treated as independent investigations.

name: Solid Surface Combustion Experiment aboard USML-1
summary: Paper describes flame spread over a thin cellulosic solid fuel in 35% oxygen / 65% nitrogen at 1 atm; observed temperatures and flame images.
insight: A surface-tension-driven convection experiment also appears under similar filename prefix STDCE-1: it is NOT SSCE and must not be merged.

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (SAME)
summary: Research report concerns modeling/simulation of smoke generation in microgravity using SAME data; accompanying combined results workbook contains experimental/smoke-generation diagnostics.
insight: Focus is fire detection and smoke characteristics, not direct flame-spread measurements.

name: Laminar Non-Premixed Flames of Gaseous Fuel Aboard the International Space Station
topic: Microgravity gaseous non-premixed laminar flames and spacecraft fire safety
oxygen_note: Tests included atmospheres with elevated oxygen concentrations (self-extinguishment found below ~25% by volume for BRE flames) and reduced pressures for future spacecraft [Pages 2, 6-7].
summary: This document reviews six independent studies of gaseous fuel flames conducted on the International Space Station (ISS) between late 2017 and early 2022 under the Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) project, alongside precursor investigations. The studies explored coflow laminar diffusion flames, electric-field effects on flames, material flammability via a burning rate emulator (BRE) simulating solid/liquid fuels, flame design and soot control, structure and response of spherical diffusion flames, and cool flames with gases. The experimental hardware utilized the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) and associated chamber inserts.
insight: Space-based microgravity research enables the elimination of buoyant convection and flicker, allowing the observation of quasi-steady, high-residence-time flames with extended length scales that reveal distinct phenomena such as enhanced soot production, unique electric field ion-current peaks, stable low-momentum burning, and non-premixed cool flames.
evidence_type: Review and summary of experimental research findings
category: Spacecraft Fire Safety; Gaseous - Premixed and Non-Premixed; Solid Fuels
